title: Concision: cutting the fat
lede: Say it in fewer words. Every word you cut makes the rest hit harder.

sections.md:
## Wordy phrases and their replacements
| Instead of | Write |
|---|---|
| in order to | to |
| due to the fact that | because |
| at this point in time | now |
| in the event that | if |
| has the ability to | can |
| make a decision | decide |
| a large number of | many |
| until such time as | until |

## Cut these on sight
- **Fillers:** just, really, very, actually, basically, kind of.
- **Throat-clearing:** "I'm writing to let you know that…", "It is important to note that…"
- **Doubles:** "each and every," "first and foremost," "true facts."

sections.title: Cut by half
sections.problem: "I just wanted to reach out to let you know that, due to the fact that our truck is in the shop, we basically won't be able to make the pickup at this point in time." (38 words)
steps: Cut the throat-clearing: "I just wanted to reach out to let you know that."
due to the fact that → because. at this point in time → today. basically → cut.
sections.answer: "Our truck is in the shop, so we can't make today's pickup." (**12 words**)

sections.label: The read-aloud rule
sections.md: Read your draft out loud. Anything you'd never say in conversation is probably padding.

practice.q: Shortest version of "in the event that":

options: We made the decision to expand.
A decision was made by us to expand.
We came to a decision regarding expansion.
